query_database.py:192-203: acquire happens before the try/finally that releases; if acquire is cancelled the lock is not held and only the entry claim is released (CPython Lock.acquire handles wake-up of the next waiter itself on cancellation). asyncio.Lock.release is synchronous, has no owner-task check, so calling it in finally during cancellation unwinding is valid. CPython Lock uses a collections.deque of waiter futures appended in arrival order and woken FIFO (with barging only by non-waiting acquirers when unlocked and no waiters). Based on known stdlib semantics; stdlib source not in the view.

query_database.py:166-203 _conversation_turn keeps one entry per conversation id with users counting holders and waiters, so a single asyncio.Lock is shared. asyncio.Lock wakes waiters in FIFO order (3.10+), which gives arrival order. send_message runs inside the lock (444-470). On CancelledError (471-482) _rollback_conversation truncates to the baseline length before the lock is released. Counterexample tried: a cancelled waiter. It releases its claim without touching the entry (194-197). A conversation_id of None is unqueued, but the agent then mints a private id, so nothing can share it (182-184, docstring 169-177). The MCP server always passes a concrete id. Cancellation during the baseline read happens before the agent adds any messages, so there is nothing to remove. Note that rollback depends on the store exposing a synchronous truncate_messages. The shipped BoundedConversationStore does, and other stores only log a warning. I did not find any history write that bypasses the lock.

query_database.py:186-203: entry created and users incremented synchronously (no await) before acquire; except BaseException around acquire (194-197) calls _release_queue_entry, which decrements and deletes the entry when users<=0 and it is still the registered one (160-162). Normal path releases in finally (201-203). Hostile input: cancelling a waiter just handed the lock. asyncio.Lock.acquire handles that by re-waking the next waiter and leaving the lock unlocked. This call's users claim is still released by the except arm, so users returns to zero once all calls finish and the entry is deleted. The unqueued None path creates no entry. The claim holds.

criteria.json read: well-formed, criterion 1 matches this claim, so it counts. Head code: Anthropic llm.py:72 uses anthropic.AsyncAnthropic; :78 awaits messages.create (non-streaming), :115 uses async with messages.stream (streaming), so neither blocks the loop. Postgres/MySQL/SQLite run_sql (postgres/sql_runner.py:129, mysql/sql_runner.py:96, sqlite/sql_runner.py:98) each await run_blocking_sql(self._run_sql_blocking...), and _run_sql_blocking contains connect (pg :138/:140, mysql :104, sqlite :107/:109), execute and fetchmany (pg :178-180, mysql :147-149), so all driver calls run on the dedicated ThreadPoolExecutor (sql_threads.py:88,146-155) while the coroutine awaits via wrap_future; the loop stays free, hence the HTTP transport can serve /healthz (I did not read transport/http.py or run a live request; this rests on the loop being unblocked). Trigger-condition split in run_blocking_sql: slot.locked() true -> waits via asyncio.wait_for (non-blocking), outside the trigger: only waits asynchronously, and on timeout (>60s) raises SqlWorkersBusyError without running, so no call is blocked in a driver call; submit failure -> slot released and raised, outside the trigger (fails closed, nothing blocked); cancellation -> outside the trigger (no longer blocked caller; thread continues, sibling criterion 10 states this). Residual loop-blocking work (to_csv, guard parsing, import_memory) is excluded by criterion 10 and is not a driver/Anthropic call. The PR itself only adds the turn queue/docs; the behavior comes from #300 already in base and present at head.

criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 2 (claim_signature issue-acceptance-2), so it counts. In head query_database.py, the only added serialization is _conversation_turn (line ~186-189, used at 444), which keys a separate asyncio.Lock entry per conversation_id in _CONVERSATION_QUEUES. Two calls with different ids get distinct entries and distinct locks, so neither acquire waits on the other; no global lock is added on the run path (get_agent's lock only guards cold start). Blocking calls are off the event loop per #300 (criterion 10 notes async Anthropic client and SQL worker pool), so both can be in their blocking calls at once. Test test_different_conversation_ids_run_concurrently (tests/unit/test_query_database_queue.py) asserts both turns entered with two gates open. Split of the code condition (conversation_id is None / entry exists / acquire failure): None -> outside the trigger (the criterion requires two different ids, and a None call takes no lock anyway); entry-exists branch -> only reached by the same id, outside the trigger (different ids); acquire BaseException -> only cancellation, outside the trigger and fails closed by releasing the entry and re-raising. The 8-thread SQL pool limit is an existing #300 bound named in criterion 10, not a new cross-conversation wait.

criteria.json counts (criterion 3 matches). query_database.py:444 wraps the whole agent run (async for agent.send_message, 467-470, which includes the agent's own history appends) in `async with _conversation_turn(conversation_id)`. _conversation_turn (166-203) keeps one asyncio.Lock per id in _CONVERSATION_QUEUES; users counts holders and waiters (190, 152-162), so no second lock is minted for a live id. The lock is released in `finally` (202) on return, failure or cancellation, so the second run starts only after the first ends. A cancelled waiter releases its claim (194-197). The cancel handler rolls back before release (471-482), so the history is the first call's messages followed by the second's. Split alternatives: conversation_id None (182-184) -> outside the trigger, since the claim needs two calls sharing an id and the agent mints a private id (server.py always passes a concrete id). Baseline-read failure (462-464) -> fails closed with RuntimeError, lock released by the context manager. Cancelled while waiting -> releases and re-raises, so the run never starts. Other exceptions (483-500) -> raise inside the context manager and release the lock.

Criteria file read (valid list; criterion 4 present). query_database.py:182-203: entry is created/incremented (186-190) with no await before the try; users counts holders and waiters. Waiter path: `except BaseException` (194-197) calls _release_queue_entry then re-raises, so a cancelled waiter leaves no entry. Holder path: `finally` (201-203) releases lock and calls _release_queue_entry on return, failure or cancel. _release_queue_entry (160-162) decrements and deletes when users<=0 and the map entry is this entry; a successor entry cannot exist while this one is still mapped, so the identity check never leaves a stale entry. Split conditions: `conversation_id is None` -> outside the trigger (no entry is ever created, so none held); `users <= 0` false -> only while another call still holds/waits, i.e. not 'every call has finished'; `is entry` false -> entry already removed, nothing stale; acquire exception (incl. cancel) -> handled at 194-197; body exception/cancel/GeneratorExit -> finally 201-203. No await between increment and acquire, so no cancel gap. Not separately graded on sibling behavior.

criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 5, so it counts. query_database.py:444-482: under the per-conversation turn lock, _conversation_baseline (206-221) reads len(conversation.messages) after earlier same-id calls finish (the lock serializes them). The agent run is wrapped in `except asyncio.CancelledError` (471), which calls _rollback_conversation (224-290) before the lock is released, then re-raises. The rollback is synchronous and calls BoundedConversationStore.truncate_messages (conversation_store.py:94-130), which deletes conversation.messages[length:] on the same Conversation object the agent appends to (agent.py:529, 701, 1048, 1105 use conversation.add_message). The next call therefore baselines and runs on the restored history. Alternatives split: (a) queued_id None (conversation_id None) skips the rollback -> outside the trigger, since the agent mints a private id no later call can name and the MCP server always passes a concrete id (server.py per docstring 166-177). (b) Missing or raising truncate_messages -> fault path that logs at ERROR and still re-raises. This applies only to non-default stores, and the default store implements it. (c) A truncate that returns False means the conversation was evicted or has nothing to drop, which is nothing to restore. (d) Cancellation during the baseline read happens before any messages are added, and the baseline `except Exception` does not catch it. No departure inside the trigger was found.
